paras: The threatened lynching of John Black took place in South Carolina in late August 1903, when Black, a Black worker at the Haile Gold Mine arrested on a charge of poisoning his wife, faced "some threats of lynching" before police locked him in the guard house at Kershaw. He was not harmed and was held to be taken to the jail at Camden.
Black was described as "colored" and as "one of the hands at Haile Gold Mine." His wife lived on Lewis Sowell's place in Kershaw county.

According to the Kershaw Era, Black visited his wife on a Sunday and gave her medicine, telling her to take it when she lay down and to lie perfectly quiet, then returned to the mine. She took the medicine on going to bed that night, began having pains, called in neighbors, went into convulsions and died during the night. Black was arrested on the charge of poisoning her.

The report states that "there were some threats of lynching" but does not say who made them, where, or whether any crowd gathered. Black was instead brought to Kershaw and turned over to policeman Catoe, who locked him in the guard house until he could be taken to Camden jail.
No report of an inquest, an indictment or a trial on the poisoning charge appears in the coverage, and nothing further is reported about the threats.

The episode is known from a single item, a Kershaw Era report reprinted in the Lancaster Ledger on August 26, 1903, under the headline "A Negro Man Charged With Poisoning His Wife." The item gave the alleged poisoning in detail and mentioned the lynching threats in a single sentence, without comment. No coverage was found in other white papers or in the Black press.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of John Black
bases: The only report says there were 'some threats of lynching' against Black after his arrest, but describes no crowd, no move on the prisoner and no injury (A1).

Black was not killed; he was placed in the town guard house to await transfer to jail, and the report names no one who made the threats and gives no number (A1). The threats were tied to the accusation that he poisoned his wife (A1).
One item, a Kershaw Era report reprinted in the Lancaster Ledger, is the only coverage found in either press (A1).

accounts.label: Kershaw Era (local report)
accounts.gist: Black was arrested for poisoning his wife; despite 'some threats of lynching' he was brought to Kershaw and locked in the guard house to await Camden jail.

framing.detail: Headline 'A Negro Man Charged With Poisoning His Wife'; the poisoning account is given in detail and the lynching threats are noted without comment.

record_check.dossier: Black is described as 'colored' and the headline calls him 'A Negro Man'

The report places the wife's home (and the alleged poisoning) 'in Kershaw county' and the planned jail at Camden; it does not say in which county the town of Kershaw lies or where the threats were made
Supported: he was under arrest and held by policeman Catoe; he was not taken from officers
Supported as late August 1903 (before 1903-08-26); the exact date is not stated

info: Late August 1903, before 1903-08-26: the wife died on a Sunday night and Black was arrested 'yesterday' relative to the Kershaw Era's (unstated) issue date; no calendar date is given
The wife lived on Lewis Sowell's place; Black was brought to the town of Kershaw and held in the guard house there
